title: Larry Rubin Asks Senate to Reject Dual Nationality Reform Promoted by Sheinbaum
author: José Shaddai Olvera Torres
content:
_This article by José Shaddai Olvera Torres originally appeared in
the[September 28, 2026 edition of El
Chamuco](https://elchamuco.com.mx/2026/09/28/larry-rubin-pide-al-senado-
rechazar-reforma-de-doble-nacionalidad-impulsada-por-sheinbaum/), Mexico's
premier left wing daily newspaper._

**Cover: Jerge**

**(September 28, 2026).—The representative of the Republican Party in Mexico
questioned limiting access to the Presidency, governorships and the Head of
Government to people with a single nationality.**

Larry Rubin, representative of the **Republican Party in Mexico** and
president of the **American Society of Mexico** , called on Mexican senators
to reject the constitutional reform promoted by President **Claudia
Sheinbaum** that seeks to establish sole Mexican nationality as a requirement
for those who aspire to the Presidency of the Republic, the governorships and
the Head of Government of Mexico City.

Through social media, Rubin asked the 128 senators to weigh their
responsibility to the citizens before voting on the initiative.

“Each senator will have to decide whether their responsibility lies first with
a party instruction or with the Mexicans they swore to represent,” he wrote.

The statement comes after the **Chamber of Deputies approved the reform with
334 votes in favor, 109 against and one abstention**. The bill was sent to the
Senate, where its discussion and vote are expected.

### Rubin Questions That Dual Nationality Determines Loyalty

The reform proposes modifying **Articles 82, 116 and 122 of the Constitution**
to establish that those who aspire to the Presidency, the governorships or the
Head of Government of Mexico City maintain an exclusive legal and political
bond with the Mexican State.

The bill establishes that those who hold another nationality must renounce it
before registering as candidates and prove that the legal bond with the other
country ceased to exist in accordance with its legislation. The measure would
begin to apply starting with the **2028** electoral process, so it would have
no effect on the 2027 elections.

> Ante la próxima votación de la reforma de la doble nacionalidad, hacemos un
> llamado urgente a cada una y cada uno de los senadores de la República.  
>  
> Esta votación va mucho más allá de los partidos.  
>  
> Cada…
>

Rubin questioned that having a second nationality could be used as a criterion
to determine a person's loyalty to Mexico.

> Dual nationality does not mean dual loyalty. Being Mexican is not measured
> by how many passports we have, it is measured by our commitment to Mexico.
>
> Larry Rubin, in a message posted on social media

The Republican representative also stated that the reform could create a
division between citizens with one and two nationalities, while asking that
consideration be given to binational families and to Mexicans who maintain
ties with the United States.

### A Position Rubin Had Already Expressed

This is not the first time Rubin has questioned the proposal. In early
September he called the initiative a **“very serious mistake”** and maintained
that having more than one passport does not determine a person's loyalty to
Mexico.

On that occasion he stated that the measure could affect millions of Mexicans
with dual nationality. The figure of potentially affected people that Rubin
has mentioned has varied and **should not be presented as official data
without a demographic source to back it up**.

For her part, Sheinbaum has defended the reform with the argument that those
who occupy the Presidency, a governorship or the Head of Government must
maintain an exclusive legal and political bond with Mexico. The president has
maintained that no head of government should have “two flags.”

### The Reform Reaches the Senate

The bill is now in the **Senate of the Republic** , where it needs a qualified
majority to amend the Constitution.

The discussion also takes place amid differences among the parliamentary
groups allied with Morena. According to recent reports, the ruling party
caucus and its allies have a narrow margin to reach the required votes.

Thus, Rubin's call adds to the public debate over the nationality requirements
to access the country's main executive offices, while the Senate prepares to
decide the future of the reform.
